completion_conditions: Each of the fourteen pairs has an assertion that fails when the sites diverge.
Every assertion names both sites and the fix in its failure message.
Every assertion runs green inside a freshly installed target, not only on the platform.
The full suite, the init suite and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: The pattern was measured, not assumed. `scripts/validate_shiki.py:1892` holds `.shiki/schemas/ledger.schema.json`'s type enum SET-EQUAL to `LEDGER_TYPES`; when a task tried to add a ledger type with only the schema in its locks, that binder failed instantly and named the fix — a cheap, loud failure. By contrast the CCA workflow's inline transport schema had NO binder against `.shiki/schemas/cca-verdict.schema.json`, and six distinct shape violations reached production over two days, each costing one to three CCA re-runs per PR. Same shape, opposite cost, and the difference is entirely whether a binder exists.

Fourteen pairs are in scope; all AGREE today, so the module is green on landing and no other file changes. Ten further pairs are already DIVERGED and are explicitly out of scope — repairing a divergence is the owning task's job, and folding repairs in here would make a test-only task carry behaviour changes.
Assertions must be SET-EQUALITY, never needle or containment, except where the audit found containment is the correct relation (the prose sites in pair 5, and the subset relation in pair 11).

Every assertion must be TARGET-VALID: it may read only artifacts that ship (`scripts/shiki_installer.py` `TEMPLATE_PATHS`) and must tolerate an empty `.shiki` mirror. `scripts/test_shiki_init.sh:383` runs the installed target's `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`, so a platform-only assertion would need a `TARGET_INSTALL_EXCLUDES` entry (`shiki_installer.py:161`) — which is outside these locks and would make the task unsatisfiable.

LOCK-SUFFICIENCY CHECK (2026-08-04). MUST-CHANGE: `tests/test_paired_invariants.py` only. Verified: `tests/test_install_completeness.py`'s `classify()` (`:130-138`) returns None for `tests/…`, so a new test file needs no `TEMPLATE_PATHS` entry; `tests` ships as a whole directory (`shiki_installer.py:41`); nothing in `scripts/validate_shiki.py` enumerates `tests/` (`:1628` pins only the `scripts/test_shiki_*.sh` sweep); `scripts/test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh` is positive-membership over `scripts/`. ONE file, and zero lock conflicts against every other backlog item.

`scripts/validate_shiki.py` is deliberately NOT locked. Binders that must run inside validate_shiki (the mirror-record loops) belong to their own repair tasks, and locking it here would collide with four other backlog items.
No new `scripts/*.py` module may be added: that would require a `TEMPLATE_PATHS` entry (`tests/test_install_completeness.py:183`) and pull `shiki_installer.py` into the locks.

Risk is medium and honest: this adds one test file. It changes no behaviour, no gate, no schema and no workflow. Under `.shiki/guardian-policy.json` (`applies_to_risk: [high, critical]`) neither the Contract PR nor the implementation PR triggers the Guardian gate.

outcome: Fourteen places where two or more artifacts must agree gain a set-equality assertion, so divergence fails immediately and loudly instead of silently. This is the single highest-recurrence defect class measured in this repository: where a pair is bound, failure is instant and cheap; where nothing binds it, failure is silent and expensive. Every pair listed agrees on the tree today, so the module lands green and changes no other file.

tasks.scope:
Add `tests/test_paired_invariants.py` with one assertion per pair below. Every pair AGREES on the tree today, so the module lands green with no other file changed. Each assertion must name BOTH sites and the fix in its failure message, in the style of `tests/test_cca_verdict_consistency.py:244-252`.

Every assertion must be TARGET-VALID: read only artifacts that ship (per `scripts/shiki_installer.py` `TEMPLATE_PATHS`) and tolerate an empty `.shiki` mirror. `scripts/test_shiki_init.sh:383` runs the installed target's `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`, so an assertion that needs a platform-only file would fail there and could not be excluded from inside these locks.

THE FOURTEEN PAIRS, ranked by silence x cost:
  1. `shiki_jsonschema.SUPPORTED_KEYWORDS` (`scripts/shiki_jsonschema.py:29-48`) vs the keywords `scripts/shiki_schema.py` actually implements (`:19,:23,:26,:39`). Assert every schema reached by `shiki_schema.validate_instance` — `cca-verdict`, `repair-packet` — uses ONLY the implemented subset, recursively. A hardening written with an unimplemented keyword validates and constrains nothing.
  2. Check-name literals: `mergegate_check.SELF_CHECKS`/`VERDICT_CHECKS` (`:27,:28`), `shiki_loop.CCA_VERDICT_CHECK` (`:56`), `shiki_evidence` (`:87`) vs the workflow job `name:` values (`shiki-cca-completion.yml:30,442`, `shiki-mergegate.yml:27`). Each literal must be a real job name.
  3. `_GENERIC_MIRROR_DIRS` (`mergegate_check.py:2148-2160`) unioned with `{tasks,goals,locks,ledger,repairs,plans}` == the manifest's `state_class: mirror` directories.
  4. Four PR-body producers — `shiki_github.github_pr_body` (`:749`), `shiki_loop._closeout_pr_body` (`:1200`), `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/shiki-task.md` — each satisfies all four headings the gate requires (`mergegate_check.py:2698`).
  5. CCA verdict values: set-equality across the schema, `enforce_cca_verdict.VALID_VERDICTS` (`:16`) and `shiki_loop.CCA_VERDICT_VALUES` (`:65`, whose comment claims it mirrors with no check); containment for the workflow and the five prose sites.
  6. Risk vocabulary: set-equality across `validate_shiki.RISK_LEVELS` (`:186`), `shiki_guardian.KNOWN_RISK_LEVELS` (`:13`), `mergegate_check._RISK_ORDER` (`:917`), the `shiki_cli.py` choices (`:157,:333,:356`) and `task.schema.json`.
  7. Code-review verdicts: set-equality across the adapter transport enum and `CODE_REVIEW_VALID_VERDICTS` (`shiki_runtime_adapters.py:201,:221`), the prompt prose (`shiki_loop.py:999-1000`) and the bare literals (`shiki_loop.py:1059,1073,1089,1696`).
  8. `DEFAULT_REQUIRED_CHECKS` (`shiki_contracts.py:21-26`) — every entry is a real workflow job name. `validate_shiki.py:1774` binds only the `config.yaml` path, never this fallback.
  9. `.shiki/schemas/memory-entry.schema.json` vs `shiki_memory.MEMORY_STATUSES` (`:30`) and `MEMORY_AREAS` (`:39-53`), set-equal; and every shipped memory record validates.
  10. `WORKFLOW_CONTRACTS` keys (`validate_shiki.py:229`), the `TEMPLATE_PATHS` `.github/workflows/*` entries and `shiki_doctor.py`'s required-file list agree.
  11. `repair-packet.schema.json`'s `required_skill` enum is a SUBSET of `validate_shiki.KNOWN_SKILLS` (subset, not equality — the audit measured the difference as empty).
  12. Every checklist id referenced outside `docs/agents/checklists.md` (`CCA-05`, `CCA-08`, `CI-08`, `CCA-01`, `CCA-12` in `enforce_cca_verdict.py`, the CCA workflow, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/*`) is defined in that document.
  13. `.shiki/config.yaml` `guardian.users`/`labels` (`:11-16`) agree with `.shiki/guardian-policy.json` `approvers.users` and `guardian_label.label`.
  14. `SMOKE_REQUIRED`/`START_REQUIRED` (`validate_shiki.py:169,:170`) set-equal with `smoke.schema.json`/`start.schema.json`.

Where a pair's correct relation is containment or subset rather than equality — pair 5's prose sites, pair 11 — assert that relation and say so in the failure message. Everywhere else assert SET-EQUALITY: a needle check passes while a site silently gains an entry the other lacks, which is the failure mode this task exists to remove.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  The measured pattern: where two artifacts must agree and something binds them, failure is immediate and cheap; where nothing binds them, failure is silent and expensive.
  Bound example: `validate_shiki.py:1892` raises `type enum must match ...` unless `.shiki/schemas/ledger.schema.json`'s type enum equals `LEDGER_TYPES`. When a task tried to register a new ledger type with only the schema in its locks, that binder failed on the first run and named the fix.
  Unbound example: the CCA workflow's inline `--json-schema` transport schema declared checklist and acceptance items as `{type: object, additionalProperties: true}` while the repository schema required named fields and types. Nothing compared them. Six distinct shape violations reached production over 2026-08-03/04 — empty `task_id`, missing acceptance evidence, `checklist[].evidence` as an array, empty `acceptance`, `null` reason, and 21 invented checklist ids — each costing one to three CCA re-runs per PR, and two PRs needed the shape pinned by hand in the PR body before they would pass.
  Second unbound example: `TEMPLATE_PATHS` versus what shipped artifacts reference. A freshly installed target could not pass its own required check, and the installer reported `target Shiki validation passed`.
  Exact change that reproduces this result: one test module asserting the fourteen agreements that hold today.
  Reproducible when: breaking any one of the fourteen agreements fails the suite with a message naming both sites and the fix.
